I found one bug in the uncommitted `clinic/evaluate.py`, at line 15. I only read the code and didn't run it.

`StratifiedKFold` splits at the visit level. `clinic/data.py` says patients have several visits and that per-patient features (age, chronic conditions) repeat across a patient's rows. So one patient's visits can land in both the train and test folds. The model can then learn a patient's repeated feature values and outcomes from their training visits and score well on their other visits. That makes the reported PR-AUC too optimistic compared with performance on new patients.

To fix it, keep `patient_id` available from `load` and split with `StratifiedGroupKFold`, passing `groups=df["patient_id"]` to `cv.split`.

I found nothing else wrong in that file.

findings.summary: StratifiedKFold splits at visit level, so the same patient's visits land in both train and test folds (patient-level leakage).
findings.failure_scenario: data.py says patients have multiple visits and per-patient features (age, n_chronic) repeat across rows. The model can memorize a patient's repeated feature values and their outcomes from training visits, then score well on that patient's other visits in the test fold. The reported PR-AUC is optimistically biased and won't match performance on new patients. Fix: carry patient_id through load/FEATURES and use StratifiedGroupKFold (groups=df['patient_id']) in cv.split.
